inputParameters.query: Signal-to-Noise Quality Indicator SNQI signal quality metric columns researchprocess

SELECT
    o.weathprofile AS weather_condition,
    ROUND(AVG(s.snrratio)::numeric, 2) AS avg_snqi,
    ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY s.snrratio)::numeric, 2) AS median_snqi,
    COUNT(*) AS analyzable_signals
FROM signals s
JOIN telescopes t ON s.telescref = t.telescregistry
JOIN observatories o ON t.observstation = o.observstation
WHERE s.snrratio IS NOT NULL
  AND o.weathprofile IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY o.weathprofile
ORDER BY avg_snqi DESC;

    o.weathprofile AS weather_condition,
    ROUND(AVG(s.snrratio)::numeric, 2) AS avg_snqi,
    ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY s.snrratio)::numeric, 2) AS median_snqi,
    COUNT(*) AS analyzable_signals
FROM signals s
JOIN telescopes t ON s.telescref = t.telescregistry
JOIN observatories o ON t.observstation = o.observstation
WHERE s.snrratio IS NOT NULL
  AND o.weathprofile IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY o.weathprofile
ORDER BY avg_snqi DESC;

messages.content:
Here are the results of the analysis.

**Assumption:** There is no column literally named `SNQI` in the database. I mapped it to `signals.snrratio` (Signal-to-Noise Ratio), which is the closest semantic match for "Signal-to-Noise Quality Indicator." Weather conditions were taken from `observatories.weathprofile`.

### SNQI by Weather Condition

| Weather Condition | Avg SNQI | Median SNQI | Analyzable Signals |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Clear | 11.48 | 12.02 | 354 |
| Cloudy | 10.23 | 10.78 | 330 |
| Partially Cloudy | 8.57 | 7.48 | 316 |

**Key takeaways:**
- **Clear** conditions produce the best signal quality on average (11.48) and also have the most analyzable signals (354).
- **Cloudy** conditions are in the middle (10.23 average).
- **Partially Cloudy** conditions show the lowest average SNQI (8.57), and notably its median (7.48) is much lower than its average, indicating a right-skewed distribution — a handful of higher-SNQI signals are pulling the average up while most signals sit lower.

args.query:
SELECT
    o.weathprofile AS weather_condition,
    ROUND(AVG(s.snrratio)::numeric, 2) AS avg_snqi,
    ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY s.snrratio)::numeric, 2) AS median_snqi,
    COUNT(*) AS analyzable_signals
FROM signals s
JOIN telescopes t ON s.telescref = t.telescregistry
JOIN observatories o ON t.observstation = o.observstation
WHERE s.snrratio IS NOT NULL
  AND o.weathprofile IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY o.weathprofile
ORDER BY avg_snqi DESC;

args.query:
SELECT
    o.weathprofile AS weather_condition,
    ROUND(AVG(s.snrratio)::numeric, 2) AS avg_snqi,
    ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY s.snrratio)::numeric, 2) AS median_snqi,
    COUNT(*) AS analyzable_signals
FROM signals s
JOIN telescopes t ON s.telescref = t.telescregistry
JOIN observatories o ON t.observstation = o.observstation
WHERE s.snrratio IS NOT NULL
  AND o.weathprofile IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY o.weathprofile
ORDER BY avg_snqi DESC;
